content.comment_body: Hello, I'm using [product_name] to control the lighting in my home. Everything is working well, but I'm interested in adding dimming functionality to two light fixtures. I believe I would need an [product_name] analog output module that provides a 0 to 10 volt signal. This signal could be connected to a converter, which would then adjust the voltage from 0-10V to normal mains voltage (100-220V). Can anyone confirm if this approach is correct? I'd also appreciate suggestions for suitable converters. Alternatively, is there another method to achieve dimming—such as with fixtures that operate at 12V via a transformer? Thank you! [user_name]
Hi, you might want to consider using an electronic control gear such as the QUICKTRONIC DIMMABLE model with a 1…10V interface, made by OSRAM. Links: [url] [url] [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: A user has successfully implemented home lighting control using [company_name] [product_name], and now wants to add dimming capabilities using analog output hardware. The user is unsure about the necessary hardware connections—specifically about using an analog output module, connecting this to suitable voltage converters, and compatibility with fixtures operating at different voltages. Another community member suggests a third-party dimmable electronic control gear as a solution, pointing to integration possibilities outside of the [company_name] ecosystem and highlighting the need for clearer integration instructions.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects that upgrading with an analog output module will enable dimming of lights and requests advice on the correct converter or hardware to use for this purpose. They are also looking for straightforward integration options to enable dimming with different types of light fixtures and voltages.
